prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1380; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Insured reports neck stiffness, no airbag deployment. Photos of both vehicles received and saved to file.

Entry 2: Third-party driver's carrier acknowledged liability in principle. Claimant reports pain in the right knee after impact and has presented to urgent care. Medical records requested with signed authorization. Claimant is represented by counsel; all further contact to be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 3: Counsel's office confirmed representation and sent a letter of representation. Requested the claimant's prior medical history for the knee and the first-visit imaging results. Estimate on vehicle repair received from the body shop and reviewed; supplement expected for hidden frame damage. Reserve reviewed and adjusted.

Entry 4: Received orthopedic evaluation report noting a meniscal tear in the right knee, with recommendation for physical therapy and possible arthroscopic procedure. Counsel has requested a demand package. Reviewing treatment timeline for consistency with the reported mechanism of injury. Referred file to the bodily injury unit for further evaluation.

Entry 5: Spoke with defense counsel regarding the status of the demand. Physical therapy ongoing; claimant reports partial improvement. Awaiting updated treatment notes and billing records before valuation. Supervisor notified of the open bodily injury exposure. Diary set for follow-up in thirty days.
